On Thursday, Nov 12, a change in ingest v2.14.0 increased the default batch size from 1 MB to 10 MB. With workers limited to 512 MiB, large batches caused them to run out of memory and crash-loop; the rollout went to all pods at once. Dashboards were stale for 3h40, until the backlog cleared at 12:27 UTC. [1]

No customer events were lost: they continued arriving in Kafka, and reconciliation matched event counts to Kafka offsets. They were processed late. [1][4]

To prevent a repeat, the team reverted the batch-size default and added a memory guard; the fix was merged and planned for canary rollout. [1][16] They’re also adding on-call alerts for consumer lag, sending config changes to a canary pool first, and raising worker memory to 1 GiB with load tests for large batches. The lag alert is in, but still being tuned because nightly backfills trigger it. [1][14]
